intro: Pick a word. See how strongly it listens to every other word. Numbers are an illustrated example.

steps.explanation: Choose a word in the sentence. Its row lights up, showing one weight per other word.
steps.label: Pick a word

steps.explanation: Bigger numbers mean stronger links. Notice how 'it' leans on 'cat' to learn who was tired.
steps.label: Find the strongest link

steps.explanation: Each row adds to one, so attention is shared out like slices of a pie.
steps.label: See the full split

takeaways: Words borrow meaning from the words they link to most.
Small words like 'it' borrow almost everything from elsewhere.
Every word spreads exactly one unit of attention across the sentence.
title: Which words does each word listen to?
